title: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': All Passengers Safe After Tanker Slams Into New Orleans Riverboat
snippet: More than 100 passengers were safely rescued after an asphalt tanker lost control and struck the American Heritage cruise ship at the Port of New Orleans, causing it to capsize.
content:
NEW ORLEANS — In what local officials are calling a "miracle on the Mississippi," all 100-plus passengers aboard a docked riverboat cruise ship have been accounted for after a massive asphalt tanker crashed into the vessel on Friday afternoon, causing it to capsize.

The incident unfolded around 12:30 p.m. when the tanker, identified as the Atlantic Asphalt, lost control and struck the American Heritage riverboat at the Port of New Orleans. According to New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno, passengers immediately began evacuating, but the ship tipped onto its side during the scramble.

A Dramatic Rescue Operation

Bystander video captured the harrowing moment the white, paddlewheel-style cruise ship listed heavily into the river as passengers waited on the exposed deck. Reports indicate that at least a dozen people tumbled into the water amidst the chaos.

A coordinated multi-agency response—including the New Orleans Police Department, Harbor Police, local fire crews, and good Samaritan vessels on the river—quickly pulled victims from the water. Emergency responders transported 32 passengers to nearby hospitals, all suffering from non-critical injuries.

"At this moment … we have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Mayor Moreno said during a Friday evening news conference. "And that is a credit to the first responders."

Authorities Investigate the Collision

American Cruise Lines, which operates the American Heritage, issued a statement on social media confirming that guests and crew had been evacuated and expressing deep concern for those affected.

The company noted that it is working in close coordination with the U.S. Coast Guard and local municipal authorities as an investigation into the cause of the collision gets underway.
